what: How a model quotes 'the first four words' of a numbered line (2026-11-22). One sub-agent (Claude Haiku class), two CUAD agreements as sealed copies, 60 line numbers: 40 where a dash, rule or bracket opens the line, 20 ordinary. It read the files and quoted by eye.
reading: Two causes of the false rejections in the first Kaggle run, not one. A dash counted as a word (2 of 60) was the cause already suspected. The larger one was not suspected: 4 of 60 quotations were of the line directly above or below the one asked for, although every line was numbered.

With six lines and about one slip in fifteen, a reader with the whole document would fail roughly one proof in three. The verifier now accepts the neighbouring line and reports the offset. A gap in a copy shifts lines by the size of the gap, so this costs detection only for a gap of a single line.
